links.outcome: Reading grade level (FKGL) of ChatGPT versus FootCareMD patient information
links.effect: ChatGPT FKGL 13.79 ± 1.22 vs FootCareMD 9.60 ± 1.24 (p < .0001); ChatGPT FRES 31.12 ± 7.86 vs 55.18 ± 7.27.
links.quote: The overall ChatGPT and FootCareMD® FKGL scores were 13.79 ± 1.22 and 9.60 ± 1.24 respectively (p < .0001), except for the pilon fracture FKGL scores (p = .09).

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient information (Flesch Reading Ease)
links.effect: ChatGPT FRES 31.12 ± 7.86 vs FootCareMD 55.18 ± 7.27 (p < .0001), indicating harder-to-read text.
links.quote: The overall ChatGPT and FootCareMD® FRES scores were 31.12 ± 7.86 and 55.18 ± 7.27, respectively (p < .0001).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT's foot and ankle surgery information readability and quality compared to standard patient education sources (FootCareMD) using standardized metrics (FRES, FKGL, DISCERN, JAMA benchmarks).
